source.title: ConceptScope: Characterizing Dataset Bias via Disentangled Visual Concepts
source.authors: Jin-Ho Choi; Hyesu Lim; Steffen Schneider; Jaegul Choo

record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse autoencoders to visual foundation-model representations and reports whether their latents recover visual concepts, extending SAE-based feature evidence to vision.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates SAE latents as visual-concept indicators, including prediction and localization. Bias-discovery and model-robustness results, as well as threshold-selection values, do not directly test the claim and are not rows. The paper filters out uninformative or entangled latents, retaining 3,103 of 32,768; this is reported in row r27.
record.test_reason: The paper uses SAEs on CLIP ViT-L/14 as a tool for dataset-bias analysis. Its §4 validation reports how well the method predicts and localizes concepts against caption and attention baselines. Each attribute's best latent is picked from 32,768 by training AUPRC, and there is no null or neuron baseline. The system is a vision encoder, not an LLM. So nothing here tests superposition, polysemanticity capacity, SAE completeness, stability or canonicity, or feature dimensionality as any version states them.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SAEs on CLIP are reliable concept extractors that beat caption baselines. They also report that ConceptScope reaches state-of-the-art bias discovery (Precision@10), finds new biases in ImageNet and other datasets, and diagnoses robustness without OOD sets. As limitations, they note that concepts are bounded by CLIP's knowledge, scores are lower on domain-specific datasets, and masks are coarse.
record.recipe_differences: Rather than testing toy networks with more features than dimensions or measuring overlap geometry, the paper trains an expanded SAE on CLIP ViT-L/14 representations and evaluates visual-concept prediction and localization.
record.method_sensitivity: Concept-prediction scores vary across datasets; performance is lower for domain-specific emotion and texture datasets. The paper also reports coarse localization and reduced performance on small objects.

fits_no_version.finding: In CLIP ViT-L/14 layer 23, the single best SAE latent per attribute predicts labelled visual attributes at mean F1 0.72 and AUPRC 0.76 across six datasets. Scores are lower on textures and emotions (F1 0.57 and 0.55). Latent masks localize ADE20K classes at AUPRC 0.399. Only about 10% of latents pass interpretability filters, and some latents respond to multiple unrelated concepts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents trained on vision-encoder representations include latents that align with human-labelled visual concepts.

record.problems: No control direction or null baseline is reported for the feature-recovery evaluations. CLIP similarity is used as pseudo-ground truth for correlation tests. Concept analysis retains only about 10% of the SAE latents after filtering; localization uses coarse patch-level masks and drops for small objects. These results concern vision representations, not LLMs or superposition geometry.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Other results, including bias-discovery scores and subgroup accuracy across 34 vision models, concern dataset bias or robustness rather than SAE feature recovery for the claim.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
No neuron polysemanticity or capacity analysis.
No LLMs; no measure of feature spread across neurons; no null or neuron baseline for SAE recovery.
No completeness, cross-seed feature matching or canonicity test. Seed std of downstream scores (0.01) is not feature stability.
No comparison of 1-D and multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3' and V4 'supports' are reversed here. V4 concerns LLMs, and this study uses SAEs as a tool in a vision encoder, picking the best latent per attribute with no null comparison. The study cites Toy Models only to say SAEs yield monosemantic latents. The reported 'std 0.01 across seeds' concerns downstream scores, not feature identity.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-over-capacity setup, overlap geometry, or sparsity-dependent transition is tested.
No neuron polysemanticity or competition for representational capacity is tested.
No alternative causes of polysemantic neurons are tested.
Tests SAE recovery of visual concepts from CLIP representations, not feature distribution in LLMs or how many neurons encode each feature.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, canonical, or stable across SAE training runs; it filters entangled latents and tests concept-prediction performance.
Uses individual SAE latent dimensions but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features or test the dimensionality of underlying model features.

rows.subject: OpenAI CLIP ViT-L/14 + ConceptScope SAE
rows.size_stated: CLIP ViT-L/14; d=1024; 32,768 SAE latent dimensions
rows.stage_stated: SAE trained on ImageNet-1K for 5 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Filtered latent dimensions for interpretability before using them for concept analysis.

conditions.value: Discard max activation never above 0.5 and concept strength above 0.1

rows.measure: Number and proportion of latent dimensions retained
rows.value: 3,103 latent dimensions; about 10% of the original set
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: The authors say some latents are not interpretable or monosemantic and may combine unrelated concepts; the filtering excludes such latents from analysis.
rows.check: This is a selection/filtering value (3,103 of 32,768 latents kept), not a result. The filters are max activation >0.5 and concept strength ≤0.1. The paper notes some latents mix unrelated concepts but gives no count of entangled latents.

rows.subject: OpenAI CLIP ViT-L/14 + ConceptScope SAE
rows.size_stated: CLIP ViT-L/14; SAE feature dimension 32,768
rows.stage_stated: Pretrained CLIP; SAE trained on ImageNet-1K
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE patch-level activation masks with ground-truth segmentation masks.
rows.measure: Segmentation-mask AUPRC
rows.uncertainty: SAE results averaged over four models trained with different random seeds, std. 0.002; error bars indicate standard deviation across 150 classes
rows.note: The text reports the scores; localization is coarse at 16 × 16 resolution and performance drops for small objects.
rows.check: ADE20K localization AUPRC (0.399) for the method against VLM attention baselines (0.098 and 0.302). This is method performance in a vision encoder.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: SAE latents predict annotated attributes across six datasets and correlate with CLIP similarity; SAE masks also localize annotated regions (r1–r28).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Textures and emotion attributes; latent filtering and small-object localization
reader_labels.reason: Performance is lower on DTD and RAF-DB, the authors filter out most latent dimensions including entangled ones, and localization is coarse with weaker performance on small objects (r2, r5, r9, r12, r17, r18, r27, r28).
